subject: Enclave hosting pipeline: request for 3rd‑party processing roster + export snapshot
messages:
From: BlueHarbor Security <security@blueharbor.io>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: third‑party processing roster + export snapshot for enclave hosting pilot

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of FinServ's vendor review for the enclave hosting pilot, our security team needs a short inventory to close the SOC/transfer review: we need a current third‑party processing roster that touches customer data for the pilot, a simple dataflow SVG showing where data egresses the enclave (if any), and a one‑page note on which partners have access to keys (KMS/HSM) or are in scope for key escrow.

Please include:
- vendor name, country of processing, role (telemetry, caching, telemetry, metrics, telemetry — list primary role), and whether they can access plaintext data
- whether any vendor stores encrypted logs off‑site and the country of storage
- egress/export snapshot: list of countries where data could leave the enclave during normal operation and during failover
- short note if any vendor uses an SSO/SCIM integration with customer metadata

If you can return a roster CSV and a quick SVG diagram by EOD CET today, that would keep us on schedule for our security gate. Attaching the FinServ intake checklist for reference.

Thanks,
Alex Rhys
Program Lead, BlueHarbor Security
security@blueharbor.io

Attachment: finserv_intake_checklist.pdf (reference stub)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T09:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Request: third‑party processing roster + export snapshot for enclave hosting pilot

Team — forwarding intake from BlueHarbor / FinServ. Core ask: roster CSV + dataflow SVG + KMS scope note by EOD CET.

Quick notes from call:
- Pilot will route a small subset of FinServ production traffic through our enclave host in eu‑west1; they want to validate no offsite plaintext processing and map export paths.
- This is timeboxed and needs an answer today; we should surface any vendors that will trigger export controls or require onshore fallback.

Kimberly — can you surface vendor roster + whether any CDN/observability vendors store logs outside EU?
Jonas — please sketch a 1‑page dataflow (SVG) showing where KV cache and telemetry touch the data path and mark egress countries.
Neha — short KMS/HSM note + who has key access (Redwood internal service accounts vs partner accounts).

I'll consolidate and send back to Alex.

—Tessa
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: BlueHarbor Security <security@blueharbor.io>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T11:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: third‑party processing roster + export snapshot for enclave hosting pilot

Hi Alex / Alex team,

Thanks — please find the initial roster and technical snapshot below (see attachments): vendor_roster_20261030.csv and enclave_dataflow_v1.svg. Highlights:

- Edge CDN (EdgeWave Inc.) — EU only for this pilot; config uses EU POPs and logs are stored in eu‑central. No plaintext storage offsite.
- Observability (Streamlyx) — transient traces routed to a short TTL bucket; logs are redacted on ingest and encrypted at rest; storage sits in eu‑west and an encrypted replication to us‑east exists for DR (this is the one item they flagged — replication is encrypted with customer‑unique keys).
- Telemetry aggregator (TelemetryOne) — processes metrics only, no request payloads; retains aggregated metrics for 30 days in eu clusters.
- Model artifacts store (ModelHub) — private redwood account; no customer PII; access limited to Redwood service accounts.

KMS/HSM note (summary):
- Primary keys held in Redwood KMS (GCP KMS for eu‑west1) with HSM protection. Key access policy: internal service accounts only; we do not share master keys with third parties for this pilot.
- For Streamlyx DR replication we use envelope encryption; Streamlyx does not hold master keys.

Attachments: vendor_roster_20261030.csv (CSV stub), enclave_dataflow_v1.svg (diagram stub), kms_scope_table.xlsx (table stub)

If you need a copy of the raw config that shows the replication policy for Streamlyx, I can pull the snippet but would prefer to avoid sending terraform state.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Programs Manager, Redwood Inference

From: BlueHarbor Security <security@blueharbor.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T13:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: third‑party processing roster + export snapshot for enclave hosting pilot

Kimberly — this is helpful, thanks. A couple quick followups to close the gate:
1) For Streamlyx DR replication to us‑east — can you confirm whether customer‑specific payloads are included in that replication or if it's only metadata/aggregates? If payloads are replicated, we need an export control assessment.
2) For the CDN logs stored in eu‑central — can you provide the retention policy (TTL) and whether any logs contain request bodies or just headers/metadata?

If either of these items is outside EU residency for customer data, we will ask for an onshore fallback during the pilot. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex Rhys
Program Lead, BlueHarbor Security
security@blueharbor.io

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: BlueHarbor Security <security@blueharbor.io>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-30T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: third‑party processing roster + export snapshot for enclave hosting pilot

Alex — quick clarifications inline:

1) Streamlyx DR replication: replication contains only encrypted aggregates and metadata (no plaintext customer payloads). Envelope encryption uses unique per‑customer data keys; master keys remain in Redwood KMS. We can provide the replay policy excerpt (redacted) if needed.

2) CDN logs retention: EdgeWave retains edge logs for 7 days by default for operational debugging; logs capture request metadata (headers, status, timing) and do not include request bodies. Access to logs is via RBAC and logs are encrypted at rest in eu‑central.

If BlueHarbor still requires onshore-only routing for the pilot, we can propose toggling the replication flag for FinServ to disable cross‑region replication (it is a per‑tenant flag).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: replay_policy_excerpt_redacted.txt (stub)
